claims.claim_text: The indexed Hans J Rehfisch is the playwright Hans José Rehfisch, who worked with OSS Morale Operations in London.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from a rare exact name, playwright occupation, London OSS context, 1891 birth year, and scholarship citing specific RG 226 records.

claims.claim_text: After emigrating to London, Hans José Rehfisch worked for the BBC before or during the period leading to his 1944 OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Für die BBC sowie in Emigrantenvereinigungen tätig
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The authoritative biography records Rehfisch's BBC work after his 1936 move to London and before describing his postwar move to New York.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare name, playwright identity, London setting, and direct OSS evidence establish the person at high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar or wartime work; the source does not prove that the BBC was his immediate predecessor or final civilian employer before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Published only as an earlier documented affiliation, not as immediate pre-OSS employment or last civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Felix Reichman is the Austrian-born librarian Felix Reichmann, who joined the Army and was assigned to OSS in Washington.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the Army and was assigned to the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A detailed institutional biography supplies Reichmann's full chronology, employers, 1944 Army entry, and direct OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from the distinctive near-exact name, librarian chronology, direct OSS assignment, and compatible foreign-personnel context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography explicitly sequences 1942 foundation employment, 1944 Army entry, and assignment to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Reichmann with double n is retained as a documented variant; the index's single-n spelling and clipped note remain preserved.

claims.claim_text: Felix Reichmann's immediate pre-OSS status was service in the United States Army, from which he was assigned to OSS in Washington.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the Army and was assigned to the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The biography explicitly links Army entry to the OSS assignment in the same chronological sentence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the distinctive name, full biographical chronology, and direct OSS assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence: Army entry followed by assignment to OSS in 1944.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Felix Reichmann's last documented civilian employer before Army service was the Carl Schurz Memorial Foundation, where he was librarian.

claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the final named civilian position before the same source's Army-entry sequence.
claims.match_notes: The organization name as found is retained; the canonical record preserves the historical full name.

claims.claim_text: Felix Reichmann worked as assistant curator and librarian at Landis Valley Museum from 1940 until November 1942.

claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly dated earlier pre-OSS employment; it preceded the Carl Schurz Foundation position and is not marked immediate.
claims.match_notes: The current successor name is retained only as an alias; the historical employer name appears in the claim.
